question.leadin: The Battle of Inchon was a major offensive in this conflict, and this war ended with the establishment of the Demilitarized Zone at the 38th Parallel.
question.text: Name this conflict that ended with an armistice dividing a namesake peninsula.
question.answerHtml: Korean War [accept “Conflict” in place of “War;” or Hanguk Jeonjaeng; or Choguk haebang chonjaeng]
question.clue: A commander on one side of this war proposed dropping 30 to 50 nuclear bombs on an opponent in order to create a radioactive wasteland and was criticized for rudeness to his country's leader at Wake Island.

swap.leadin: Operation Paul Bunyan involved the use of overwhelming military force to chop down a tree in this area.
swap.text: Name this area which separates North and South Korea from each other. The Joint Security Area within this zone is used for diplomatic meetings.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a certain class of warship.
question.text: An earlier example of an ironclad warship was this type of ship developed by Admiral Yi Sun-sin to resist a 16th century Japanese invasion of Korea. Named for the shape of the animal on its bow, these ships boasted cannons and a hull covered in spikes.
question.clue: Soldiers from Ming China helped defend Korea from Japanese invasion at the end of the 16th century. During that conflict, Korean Admiral Yi utilized these crazy awesome vessels which received their name from the appearance caused by their armored decks.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about yellow ribbons in history.
swap.text: Victims of the Sewol ferry disaster in this country are commemorated with yellow ribbons. The Miracle on the Han River refers to massive growth in this country's capital of Seoul.
swap.answerHtml: South Korea [or the Republic of Korea; or ROK; prompt on Korea; reject “North Korea” or the “Democratic People’s Republic of Korea”]
swap.clue: This country's first female leader led it from 2013 until her 2017 impeachment.

question.text: During the lead up to this time period, the forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei used fire ships to turn back the much larger force of Cao Cao at the Battle of Red Cliffs. This time period followed the collapse of the Han dynasty.
question.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

swap.text: Admiral Yi's decisive victories at Myeongyang and Noryang defended this peninsula from a Japanese invasion. The northern half of this peninsula, divided by a demilitarized zone since 1953, is ruled by the Kim family.
swap.clue: The "Three Kingdoms" of this region included Baekje, Silla, and Goguryeo.

question.leadin: Operation Paul Bunyan took place in this area as a result of an axe murder incident.
question.text: Name this heavily fortified strip of land created in July 1953. An armistice was signed in Panmunjom ["pan-moon-jum"], a village within this area.
question.answerHtml: Demilitarized Zone (or DMZ; prompt on Joint Security Area or JSA; prompt on North Korea–South Korea border, but do NOT REVEAL this)
question.clue: This no-man's-land along the 38th parallel. It was created in a July 1953 armistice.

swap.leadin: This leader was referred to as "supreme leader", as well as "Dear Leader" and "Generalissimo"
swap.text: Identify this leader of North Korea from 1994 to 2011. He died on December 17, 2011 of a heart attack.
swap.clue: His "Sunshine policy" tried to bolster the software industry, and he once abducted a movie director to shoot a socialist Godzilla flick.

question.text: In 1976, US forces were raised to DEFCON 3 after two army officers were killed with an ax after trying to trim a poplar tree on this country's soil. This was the only non-Middle Eastern country George W. Bush deemed to be part of an "axis of evil" during a State of the Union Address.
question.clue: One leader threatened this country with "fire and fury like the world has never seen."

swap.leadin: The nickname for this policy supposedly came from a line in an Aesop fable titled for the "North Wind."
swap.text: Name this policy instituted by Kim Dae-Jung. This policy attempted to de-escalate tensions between North and South Korea and eventually end North Korea's nuclear program.
swap.answerHtml: Sunshine Policy [or Reconciliation and Cooperation Policy Towards the North; or Operational Policy Towards the North; or Embracing Policy]
swap.clue: The adoption of this policy led to the joint operation of the Mount Gumgang Tourist Region and the Kaesong Industrial Park.

question.text: Both the Korean War and the Pueblo incident were ended by negotiations in this central Korean village on the Kyongui road.
question.clue: This village which hosted a more famous conference that led to the armistice between United Nations forces and communists in 1953 during the Korean War.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Joseon dynasty.
swap.text: This fourth and arguably greatest king of the Joseon dynasty is revered for creating the Korean writing system of Hangeul.
swap.clue: Under the guidance of his father, this man launched an expedition against a polity controlled by So Sadashige that had become a base for pirates; that assault on Tsushima was the Oei invasion.

question.leadin: These campaigns are sometimes called the "Ceramic Wars" because potters were kidnapped and moved to Arita, where they developed one country's porcelain industry.
question.text: Name these campaigns during which soldiers reportedly cut off the noses of their victims as trophies because heads were too unwieldy to haul around.
question.answerHtml: Japanese invasions of Korea [accept Hideyoshi’s invasions of Korea; accept Imjin Wars]
question.clue: That one of these events eventually ended at the Battle of Noryang.

swap.text: Members of this Joseon noble, scholarly class were expected to be knowledgeable in the Confucian classics. To enter this class, one had to perform well on the gwageo civil service exam.
swap.clue: Seowon [suh-wun] were private schools constructed for the education of this class, which was wealthier than the sangmin [sahng-meen]. A genealogy book called a jokbo [choke-boh] could be used to prove one's membership in this Korean class.

question.leadin: It arose from a state founded by Hyokkose under its efficient military, the Hwarangdo.
question.text: Name this dynasty which allied with Tang China to bolster its seventh to tenth century rule over Korea.
question.clue: This dynasty employed a cultured class of cosmetic-using soldiers called the "flowering knights," or "hwarang."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about naval engagements in Asian history.
swap.text: Japan's own attempts at navy-driven expansionism met with similar disaster after the turtle ships of this revered Korean admiral bested the fleet of Toyotomi Hideyoshi at the Battle of Noryang Point.
swap.clue: This admiral was undefeated in all naval engagements, although he died during the Battle of Noryang, which saw the Japanese finally repelled.

question.leadin: Guerrillas in this uprising set up bases in the caves around Hallasan, an extinct volcano where remains of victims can still be found, and attacked paramilitary troops of the Northwest Youth League.
question.text: Name this massacre that lasted over a year from April 1948 to 1949, in a nation being occupied under Operation Blacklist Forty.

swap.text: Original language term required. The Hanjungrok claims that Crown Prince Sado suffered from a "phobia" of this clothing, often burning many outfits. Modern examples of this traditional class of clothing were modeled on Joseon-era outfits.

question.leadin: Now located at the National Library of France, it was composed by the Buddhist monk Baegun around 1372 AD, and published by his students Seoksan and Daldam. FTPE.
question.text: Name this two-volume Korean anthology of Zen Buddhist teachings which is the oldest existing metal-plate printed book.

swap.leadin: This man's date with the bottom of the ocean in 1973 may have been averted through the quick action of ambassador Philip Habib, whom he later credited with helping to inspire his Nobel-winning Sunshine Policy.
swap.text: Identify this politician who failed thrice in his bid for the Presidency when not enduring hunger strikes, house arrests, or exile, prior to becoming the first Jeolla native to achieve the office.
swap.clue: Pope John Paul II interceded to save this man from being executed after the Gwangju People's Uprising.
